newsitem.title: USA: Kessler - 30 years too late for tobacco immunity.
newsitem.headline: Kessler - 30 years too late for tobacco immunity.

text.p: Former Food and Drug Commissioner David Kessler said Tuesday it was "30 years too late" for the tobacco industry to expect limited liability from potential lawsuits.
"Limited liability secures the industry's future. The number of potential lawsuits is enormous. It has brought them to the table," he told Reuters at the annual Cruttenden Roth Healthcare Conference.

"You don't trade public health for immunity. If there was a time for immunity it was 30 years ago when the first questions were raised about their product - not after the industry set out on the course they set out on. It's 30 years too late," he said.
He declined to comment when asked whether he was referring to alleged industry concealment of studies showing the addictiveness of tobacco.
Kessler who served as FDA commissioner from 1990 until last March, strengthened regulation of marketing and sales of tobacco to children and was an unpopular figure with many people in the industry.

Kessler said ongoing negotiations between the tobacco industry leaders, lawyers and government officials "should be re-focused on public health, on the number of people who are addicted and who smoke."

"I am not opposed to a settlement, but don't think that giving the industry immunity is the right thing to do. I think the public needs to be the winner here, not the lawyers and the tobacco industry," Kessler added.

Numerous tobacco companies are now facing a barrage of lawsuits from smokers as well as 29 attorneys general of various states suing to recover the cost of providing Medicaid funded care for cancer and other diseases they link to smoking.
"Right now you have a negotiating table being driven primarily by financial interests of people around a table. Something is wrong with that," he said.
Kessler, who was appointed by President Bush and re-appointed by President Clinton, will become Dean of the Yale School of Medicine on July 1.
